name: voidmago
description: The keeper of the Void family: the registry of which versions work together, the installer it compiles from them, and the updater that never acts silently.

vendors.name: cJSON
vendors.note: The same parser every other Void repository vendors, compiled in here rather than found on the machine. Built with CJSON_HIDE_SYMBOLS so it exports nothing: `mago` is statically linked into nothing, but the habit is what keeps six copies of one library from meeting in somebody else's binary.

interacts_with.note: Mago reads every Void project's root manifest. That is the whole dependency: it resolves the family, it does not link it. This wildcard edge is excluded from blast-radius reporting -- reading a manifest is not a contract that can break, and nothing is downstream of the reading. A project that names Mago BACK, as FaultSack does, is a different matter: it parses the schema Mago defines, and it is a retest when Mago changes.

release.summary: off Windows, the feed names the archive that actually exists, so `feed --artifacts` can hash it

behavior_changes.what: installer_name() and stable_installer_name() now answer `<Base>-<version>-<platform>.tar.gz` and `<Base>-<platform>.tar.gz` for every non-Windows platform, where they answered `<Base>-<version>-<platform>-setup` with no extension. Windows is unchanged (`-setup.exe`). The old name was a file nobody built, so `feed --artifacts` hashed nothing and wrote `"sha256": null` for Linux.
behavior_changes.who_is_affected: any application listing a non-Windows platform in `platforms`. Void Hormiga is the one today: its 0.1.3 feed carried a Linux entry with no sha256, and its Linux client refused the update. Put the runner's .tar.gz archives into the `--artifacts` directory before running `mago feed`.

update.note: Mago updates itself by the same rule it applies to everything else: the person is told, and chooses. The CLI carries no dependencies at all -- not even Void Core -- and links its C++ runtime statically, because the tool that repairs a broken install must not need a working install to run.
